title: Hack.lu CTF 2026
summary:
Hack.lu CTF is an internationally recognized, jeopardy-style cybersecurity competition organized annually by the FluxFingers team alongside the Hack.lu security conference in Luxembourg.

For the 2026 edition, I competed alongside ROTACTF (part of the Atatürk University ROTA club). We secured 49th place globally, finishing with 1,779 points across 22 challenge solves. Our run required heavy lifting in Reverse Engineering, successfully clearing complex challenges including Vaulty, VeryMildHidden, and License Validation Suite. It was a highly technical event that thoroughly tested our reversing capabilities and team coordination.

title: Hack The Box Cyber Apocalypse CTF 2026
summary:
Hack The Box Cyber Apocalypse CTF is one of the largest and most competitive annual global cybersecurity events.

For the 2026 edition, I competed with team AltayCTF and we achieved a definitive "Full Clear." We successfully captured all 136 flags across 74 scenarios, finishing with 69,900 points and securing 69th place on the global leaderboard. Clearing the entire board required us to successfully conquer every single category, including Forensics, Web, OSINT, Pwn, Coding, Reversing, Crypto, and Blockchain. This complete sweep was a massive test of our endurance, technical versatility, and seamless team coordination.

title: HackTheBox Holmes CTF 2026
summary:
Hack The Box Holmes CTF is a globally recognized and highly competitive cybersecurity challenge.

For the 2026 edition, I competed with team AltayCTF and we achieved a definitive "Full Clear," successfully solving all 111 challenges. We secured 22nd place on the global leaderboard out of a massive field of 5,636 teams. Clearing the entire board was a major milestone that required comprehensive technical capabilities and relentless team coordination across all categories.

title: K17
summary:
k17 CTF is an intense cybersecurity competition requiring precise technical execution across multiple domains.

I competed with team AltayCTF, and we secured 9th place globally with a total of 5,617 points. As an individual contributor under the handle Moltrax, I successfully captured 6 flags, contributing 777 points to our final score. My personal solves included clearing five "hard" difficulty challenges (ihyh, huge binary 2, not json, blowfish, and crivail) along with one "easy" challenge (discord). It was a rigorous event that heavily tested my ability to break down high-difficulty problems under pressure.

title: Kaspersky{CTF}
summary:
Kaspersky{CTF} is a competitive, industry-backed cybersecurity event organized by Kaspersky, challenging participants across various advanced security domains.

In the 2026 edition, we secured 12th place overall in the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa (META) region, and ranked 5th nationally in Turkey.

title: NSS
summary:
NSS CTF is a competitive international cybersecurity challenge that tests participants across multiple technical domains.

In the 2026 edition, we secured 21st place globally out of a highly competitive field of 890 teams.

title: PwnSec CTF 2026
summary:
PwnSec CTF is a highly competitive international cybersecurity challenge that tests practical exploitation and problem-solving skills across various security domains.

In the 2026 edition, I competed with team AltayCTF, securing 16th place globally with 4,789 points, capturing 85 flags and earning 1 First Blood. Individually, I ranked 100th globally, capturing 39 flags and contributing 1,312 points to our final standing.

title: UIUCTF
